channel.title: Hyundai recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Hyundai Kona Rear Center Seat Belt Buckle May Fail
item.description: Some Hyundai Kona and Kona Electric vehicles have a seat belt buckle in the rear center seat that may not properly hold a passenger in place if the vehicle is in a crash. This means that seat position may not provide the protection a seat belt is supposed to give during a collision.

item.title: Hyundai Ioniq 5 Battery Cells Risk Fire
item.description: Certain Hyundai Ioniq 5 vehicles have high voltage battery cells that may contain misaligned electrodes inside them. This kind of misalignment inside the battery can lead to a fire, and this can happen whether the vehicle is parked or being driven at the time.

item.title: Hyundai Tucson Instrument Panel Display Can Fail
item.description: Hyundai is recalling certain Tucson, Tucson Hybrid, and Tucson Plug-In Hybrid vehicles. A software error may cause the instrument panel display to fail. This display shows things like the speedometer and warning lights, so when it fails, that information may not be shown to the driver. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet a federal safety standard for vehicle controls and displays.

item.title: Hyundai SUVs: Automatic Braking May Trigger Unexpectedly
item.description: Hyundai is recalling certain 2025-2026 Santa Cruz, Tucson, Tucson Hybrid, and Tucson Plug-In Hybrid vehicles. Software in the front cameras may cause the forward collision avoidance system to turn on too early. When this happens, the system unexpectedly applies the brakes on its own, even when it isn't needed. This is a software problem in the camera that watches for collisions.

item.title: Hyundai Ioniq 5 Rear Suspension Fasteners May Detach
item.description: The fasteners holding the rear suspension on some vehicles may loosen and detach. If this happens, it can result in a loss of vehicle control.

item.title: Hyundai Elantra Hybrid Power Unit May Overheat
item.description: Some Hyundai Elantra Hybrid vehicles have a part called the hybrid power control unit, which is part of the hybrid drive system. This unit may overheat during normal use of the vehicle. Hyundai is recalling these vehicles so dealers can update the software to fix the overheating issue. The software update is meant to prevent the unit from getting too hot while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Hyundai Elantra N Airbag Deployment May Be Delayed
item.description: On certain Hyundai Elantra N, Tucson, Tucson Hybrid, Tucson Plug-In Hybrid, and Elantra vehicles, the side-impact sensors in the B-pillar may have been put together incorrectly, which can delay the airbags from deploying.

item.title: Genesis and Hyundai Seat Belt Anchors May Detach
item.description: The seat belt anchors for the driver and front passenger may come loose from the vehicle. If an anchor detaches, the seat belt will not properly hold the occupant in place during a crash, which raises the risk of injury. Dealers will inspect the anchors and reinforce or replace them as needed, free of charge.

item.title: Hyundai Ioniq 5/9: Loose Battery Bolt Fire Risk
item.description: A bolt connecting parts inside the vehicle's high voltage battery system may not be tightened properly. This can lead to an electrical short inside the battery system.

item.title: Hyundai Tucson Hybrid Instrument Display May Fail
item.description: On certain Tucson Hybrid, Tucson Plug-In Hybrid, and several other Hyundai models, a software error can cause the instrument panel display to fail. Because this display is required to function properly under the federal safety standard for vehicle controls and displays, a failure means the vehicle no longer meets that requirement.

item.title: Hyundai Palisade Third-Row Airbag May Deploy Wrong
item.description: Some Hyundai Palisade SUVs have side curtain airbags for the third-row seats that may not deploy correctly in a crash. These airbags are meant to help protect third-row passengers, but in some vehicles they may not work the way they're supposed to. Hyundai has already begun mailing letters to owners about this safety risk. Dealers will install a protective film over the rear window and remove certain padding where needed, at no cost to you.

item.title: Hyundai Tucson Tow Hitch Wiring Lets In Water
item.description: Some Tucson SUVs came with an optional tow hitch wiring harness that may have been installed incorrectly. That mistake can let water get into a control module connected to the trailer wiring. If enough moisture builds up over time, it may cause the trailer lights to stop working properly, or it may cause an electrical short circuit somewhere in the wiring connected to the hitch.

item.title: Hyundai Santa Fe rearview camera image may not display
item.description: Hyundai is recalling certain Santa Fe and Santa Fe Hybrid vehicles. The rearview camera may not have been installed correctly. A camera fitted the wrong way can damage the wiring that connects it, and the camera image may then fail to appear on the screen. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety standard for rear visibility. Dealers will replace the camera wiring harness.

item.title: Hyundai Santa Fe, Tucson Air Bags May Not Deploy
item.description: Hyundai is recalling certain 2025 Tucson, and 2025-2026 Santa Cruz, Santa Fe, and Santa Fe Hybrid vehicles because the side curtain air bags may not have been installed correctly. This can cause the air bags not to deploy the way they are supposed to in a crash. Dealers will reinstall the side curtain air bags correctly, at no cost to owners.

item.title: Hyundai Ioniq 5 Seat Belt Retractors Not Secured
item.description: On some Hyundai Ioniq 5 vehicles, the seat belt retractors for the driver and front passenger seats may not be securely fastened. A retractor that isn't properly secured may not work the way it's supposed to if the vehicle is in a crash.

item.title: Hyundai Sonata Fuel Tank Damage Risk of Fire
item.description: Hyundai says a damaged check valve in some Sonata vehicles can let air get into the fuel tank. That extra air can make the tank expand, and the expanded tank can touch hot parts of the exhaust system. Contact with the hot exhaust can melt the fuel tank, so Hyundai is having dealers check the check valve, fuel tank, and engine control software.

item.title: Hyundai Santa Fe Starter Cover Risks Electrical Short
item.description: Hyundai is recalling certain Santa Fe vehicles because the cover over the starter motor's positive battery terminal may not have been installed correctly at the factory. If the vehicle is ever involved in a crash, this improperly installed cover could allow an electrical short to occur in the wiring near the starter motor, which raises the chances of a vehicle fire starting after that kind of impact.

item.title: Hyundai Ioniq 6 charging port door may detach
item.description: This recall affects certain Hyundai Ioniq 6 electric vehicles. The panel that covers the charging port may come loose and fall off the car. Once it detaches, it can end up in the road, creating a hazard for other vehicles driving nearby.

item.title: Hyundai Palisade seat belt buckles may not latch
item.description: Hyundai is recalling certain Palisade SUVs because seat belt buckles may fail to latch. The problem affects the buckles for the driver's seat, the front passenger seat and the two second-row window seats. Dealers will replace the buckle assemblies. The replacement parts are being released in stages, so owners are being notified about the problem first and will receive a second letter when the repair is available for their vehicle.

item.title: Hyundai Ioniq 5 Recalled for Loose Suspension Bolts
item.description: Certain bolts that adjust the alignment of the rear suspension on some vehicles may not have been tightened properly.

item.title: Hyundai Tucson, Santa Fe Engine Bolts May Loosen
item.description: On certain Tucson and Santa Fe models, the bolts holding the engine's connecting rods together may not have been tightened correctly. Hyundai says this can cause the engine to lose drive power and become damaged, and in some cases the engine may begin leaking oil as a result.

item.title: Hyundai Ioniq 5 Battery Wiring May Cause Fire
item.description: Hyundai is recalling certain Ioniq 5 vehicles because the high voltage battery system may contain a bus bar that was not tightened properly, which can cause a short-circuit.

item.title: Hyundai Ioniq 5 Headlight Aim Label Wrong
item.description: On certain 2025 Hyundai IONIQ 5 vehicles, the right-side headlight may have an incorrect aim label attached, which can result in the headlight being aimed incorrectly.

item.title: Hyundai Palisade Oil Pump Fire Risk
item.description: Some Hyundai Palisade vehicles have an electric oil pump controller with an insufficient seal. This can let moisture build up on the circuit board inside, which can cause an electrical short and result in a fire.

item.title: Hyundai Ioniq 5 N Brake and Acceleration Software Flaw
item.description: Hyundai is recalling certain Ioniq 5 N vehicles that have the left-foot braking and N e-shift features. Software in the electronic brake system and vehicle control unit may cause the brakes to work less effectively whenever left-foot braking is turned on. On top of that, if the N e-shift feature is active, the car may keep accelerating on its own even after the driver takes their foot off the gas pedal, instead of slowing down as expected.

item.title: Hyundai Ioniq 5 Rear Air Bag May Not Deploy
item.description: A wiring problem in the rear floor of the vehicle may create a break in the circuit. This can cause the rear side air bag to fail to deploy the way it is supposed to in a crash.

item.title: Hyundai Ioniq 5 N: Left-Foot Braking May Weaken
item.description: On vehicles with the left-foot braking feature, software in the electronic brake and vehicle control systems may cause weaker braking when that feature is used. This can mean the vehicle needs more distance to stop.

item.title: Hyundai Rearview Camera May Fail To Display
item.description: Certain Hyundai vehicles have a damaged printed circuit board in the rearview camera. Because of this, the rearview camera image may fail to display. This means the vehicle does not meet a federal safety standard for rear visibility.

item.title: Hyundai Tucson and Santa Cruz Can Roll Without Brake
item.description: On certain new Tucson and Santa Cruz models, a wiring assembly near the console may be routed incorrectly. This can let the gear shifter be moved out of Park without the brake pedal being pressed. Dealers will reroute the wiring correctly. In the meantime, Hyundai is telling owners to use the parking brake whenever they park.

item.title: Hyundai Ioniq 5, Ioniq 6, Genesis GV60 Charging Unit Failure
item.description: Certain Hyundai Ioniq 5, Ioniq 6, and Genesis GV60 vehicles have an Integrated Charging Control Unit that may become damaged. When this happens, the unit can stop charging the 12-volt battery. If the 12-volt battery is not being charged, the vehicle can lose drive power.

item.title: Hyundai Santa Fe Sunshade Switch May Close Unexpectedly
item.description: Hyundai is recalling certain Santa Fe and Santa Fe Hybrid vehicles because the switch knob for the rear overhead sunshade may not sit fully recessed as it should. Because the knob isn't fully recessed, it can be bumped in a way that closes the sunshade when nobody meant for it to close.

item.title: Hyundai Nexo Fuel Tank Fire Risk
item.description: A safety part on the hydrogen fuel tank that releases pressure may break. If it breaks, hydrogen gas can leak out, which can start a fire while the vehicle is parked. Hyundai will replace this part to fix the problem.

item.title: Hyundai Tucson Missing Air Bag Warning Label
item.description: Certain 2025 Hyundai Tucson vehicles may be missing the air bag warning label that is supposed to be placed inside the glove box. This label is meant to warn people about the added risks an air bag can pose to an infant or a child in the front seat. Some of these vehicles may have left the factory without this label in place.

item.title: Sonata Brake Lights May Flash Incorrectly
item.description: On certain Sonata vehicles, a software issue may cause the brake lights to flash and not illuminate properly. Brake lights that don't work correctly can confuse other drivers on the road, which increases the risk of a crash.

item.title: Hyundai Santa Fe Wiring Damage May Affect Airbags
item.description: Hyundai is recalling certain Santa Fe and Santa Fe HEV vehicles because a wiring harness under the floor may rub against the second-row bench seat and become damaged. This damage could cause the airbags to go off when they are not supposed to, or it could prevent the airbags from deploying in a crash.

item.title: Hyundai, Genesis Fuel Pump May Cause Power Loss
item.description: Certain Hyundai and Genesis vehicles, including the Veloster N, Genesis G70, Elantra N, and Kona N, may have a fuel pump that fails. If the fuel pump fails, the vehicle can lose engine power while being driven. Some owners were sent an early letter warning them about this safety risk before the full notice with the repair information went out.

item.title: Hyundai Santa Fe Recalled for Rollaway Risk in Park
item.description: A software error in the transmission control unit may cause the vehicle to roll away even when it has been shifted into Park.

item.title: Hyundai Tucson, Santa Cruz may lose power steering assist
item.description: On some 2024 Hyundai Tucson and Santa Cruz vehicles, a circuit board inside the power steering system can short circuit. If this happens, the vehicle loses power steering assist, which means the steering wheel becomes much harder to turn. Dealers will replace the power steering electric power pack at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Hyundai Elantra, Kona and Venue may lose drive power
item.description: Hyundai is recalling certain Elantra, Venue, and Kona vehicles because of a problem with a part of the exhaust system called the exhaust gas recirculation valve. An electrical short circuit can happen inside this valve assembly, and when that happens the vehicle can lose drive power. A dealer will replace the exhaust gas recirculation valve assembly at no cost to the owner. Hyundai mailed letters to owners about this recall, and the company has a customer service line for questions.

item.title: Hyundai Ioniq 6 Differential Gear Bolts May Loosen
item.description: The bolts in the differential gear drive unit may not have been tightened properly. If they loosen, the vehicle could lose drive power, or the differential could lock up while driving.
